newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges restraint in Ecuador's political crisis.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges restraint in Ecuador's political crisis.

text.p: The United States said on Friday it had urged both sides in Ecuador's political crisis to show restraint and believed the country's constitution should be respected.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns was speaking to reporters after Ecuador's legislature dismissed President Abdala Bucaram on Thursday, saying he was mentally unfit to rule. Bucaram has vowed to stay in office.
Burns, accompanying Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on a trip to Houston, said: "Our view is that the constitution ought to be respected. We have counselled restraint on both sides."
But Burns said the United States took no position on whether Bucaram should stay or go. "We are not going to interpret the constitution," he said.
Burns said Washington supported the aims of a trip to Ecuador this week by Cesar Gaviria, Secretary General of the Organisation of American States who is seeking to mediate in the crisis.
"What the United States wants to see is stability, order and constitutional rule in Ecuador," Burns said.
